subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm aiming for a compact but detailed module around 400-600 lines, designing a hover vehicle with no wheels—four hover thruster pods replacing wheel positions, plus a militarized look with a roof turret, armor plates, neon underglow, light bar, antenna, and SVG decals like hazard stripes and an emblem.

Now I'm working out the chassis root and dimensions, planning hover thruster pods and landing skid feet that touch the ground, then building the lower hull with a loft from rear to front and figuring out a custom cyberpunk paint job with gunmetal tones, noise, and grime instead of using a stock panelled kit.

Planning the part budget around 150 pieces and about five textures (hazard stripes, emblem, license plate, neon kanji decal, screen), then setting up imports and helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and mirrored part placement, with a gunmetal body color and magenta cyberpunk accents.

Now I'm defining the hull's layered construction from underbody tub through lofted body sections at different z-positions, blending widths and heights to form a smooth catmull-rom curved silhouette.

Then I'm placing the cab, roof, windscreen, hood frustum shape, and truck bed with mounted rail gun turret, roof light bar, and antenna, before positioning four hover pod nacelles with ducted-fan cylindrical housings near each corner.

Each pod gets a glowing cyan disc underside, torus ring, and spinning fan blades connected to the hull via pylons and hinge joints. I'm also adding retracted landing skid legs with foot pads, a rear thruster bell pair pointing backward with glow, thin magenta underglow strips along the sides, and now I'm starting on the armor plating details.

Now I'm layering on hazard-decal side plates, skirts, a spiked bull bar, ERA bricks, and smoke launchers, plus a turret with yaw/pitch joints, glowing railgun rails, coil rings, and a shield plate. I'm texturing doors with emblem decals, kanji text, and number plates using planar geometry facing outward, then adding cyan headlight slits, red tail light strips, mirrors, exhaust vents, and considering a hanging neon sign on the rear bed.

I'm placing a small glowing "BLADE" neon sign on the bed, adding ammo crates with glowing handles, and skipping a driver model. I'm deciding joints should follow role-based naming, simplifying doors to panel seams rather than full hinges, and now working out precise z-coordinates for the bed, cab, and hood sections along with roof height and a tilted windshield box.

Now I'm defining the paint functions for the hull and armor, blending base colors with noise, adding grime toward the bottom via a smoothstep gradient, and giving the top a subtle sheen, with armor using a different seed and palette.

I'm adding thin panel seam lines on side faces using fractional patterns, then designing SVG decals: a yellow/black diagonal hazard stripe pattern, a magenta hexagon emblem with a lightning bolt and "HX-7" text, and swapping risky CJK text for a bold monospace "HOVER-OPS" label instead.

Now I'm sketching out a "NEON" text decal and a "H0V3R 2077" license plate, planning to use transparent PNG textures on plane geometry for cutouts. I'm also laying out the turret's yaw and pitch joints with their attached parts, and setting up spin joints for each hover pod's fan.

Working out blade rotation math...

Now I'm planning the fan housing: a glow disc beneath the blades, a ring torus rotated into the XZ plane, and a lathed shell for the housing with inner and outer radius profiles.

Then I'm connecting the hull to the landing pads using boxed-section rods, and positioning the pads symmetrically on either side of the chassis.

Adding skid pads with underglow strips for neon accents, then thinking through how to loft the hull cross-section—considering whether to use rounded boxes or frustum shapes for the body profile.

Still writing frustum body geometry...

Adding bull bar spikes, grille with glowing slits, roll cage with lightbar glow, antenna and dish on roof, then writing the mirrored build helper function and checking that glow effects only apply to flat-colored or textured parts, not painted ones. Now I'm designing a neon sign texture with magenta text for the vehicle.

Working out the rear thruster geometry with lathe profiles for the exhaust bells, glow discs for the nozzles, and the railgun turret assembly with rails, coil rings, and a rotating yaw/pitch base, while nailing down the exact height placements for the pedestal and joints.

I'm now checking clearances — the railgun's pitch joint needs to sit high enough (around y 2.2) so the barrel clears the cab roof when rotating, which means raising the pedestal height to about 1.3–2.0 and adjusting the rail length so the muzzle extends forward without clipping the roof.

With the geometry settled, I'll move to writing the final code efficiently, adding a few flourishes — a swept cable from turret to ammo bed, extruded stabilizer fins at the rear — to give it some mechanical detail without overcomplicating things.

Writing extrusion code...
